AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: For the early identification of patients at risk of developing diabetic nephropathy, we have developed an ultra-sensitive immune complex transfer enzyme immunoassay (ICT-EIA) to measure adiponectin in urine.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We developed ICT-EIA for adiponectin and measured urinary adiponectin from 70 healthy subjects, 35 obese non-diabetic subjects and 20 patients with diabetes.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The urinary adiponectin levels in patients with diabetes (3.3 ± 10.7 ng/mg creatinine) were significantly higher than those in obese subjects (0.54 ± 0.44; p < 0.01) and healthy subjects (0.46± 0.42; p < 0.001). The gel filtration elution profile of urine from healthy subjects showed traces of four immunoreactive peaks (high, medium, low molecular weight and monomer molecules; HMW, MMW, LMW, MM), despite the majority of blood adiponectin being HMW. However, urinary adiponectin molecules were more frequent in LMW as the estimate glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decreased. Furthermore, as blood glucose levels rose, MMW and HMW increased in urine. Further, urinary adiponectin levels correlated with eGFR (r=-0.61, p<0.001), but not urinary albumin. In addition, ou analysis showed a significantly (p<0.001) higher value for urinary adiponectin in the G2 stage of CKD classification where urinary albumin is not elevated.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Adiponectin increases in urine as renal function decreases and urinary adiponectin may be useful as a surrogate marker for diabetic nephropathy risk. Key words: enzyme immunoassay, adiponectin, urine, diabetes, surrogate marker, diabetic nephropathy.
